title: Bharti Airtel Profit Rises 31% but Misses Forecasts on Higher Costs
excerpt: Airtel's Q2 FY27 net profit of Rs 8,888 crore beat last year but fell short of the Rs 9,673 crore analysts expected, as network costs rose 11% and licence fees 13%.
body:
• Bharti Airtel reported consolidated net profit of Rs 8,888 crore for the quarter ended September 30, 2026 (Q2 FY27), up about 31% from Rs 6,792 crore a year earlier, according to Reuters and Forbes India.
  • The result missed expectations: analysts on average expected Rs 9,673 crore, according to LSEG-compiled data cited by Reuters, as network operating costs rose 11% and licence fees rose 13%.
  • Revenue from operations rose 16.7% to Rs 60,878 crore and average revenue per user rose to Rs 271 from Rs 256 a year earlier, the company reported.
  • For Airtel customers and investors: the growth came from premiumisation, not a tariff hike — Airtel added a record 1.2 million postpaid customers in the quarter, taking its postpaid base to 31.2 million.

Profit up, but below what analysts expected

India's second-largest telecom operator, Bharti Airtel, posted a smaller-than-expected second-quarter profit on Thursday as higher network operating costs offset gains from subscriber additions and users upgrading to costlier plans, Reuters reported.

The company's consolidated net profit rose to Rs 88.88 billion (Rs 8,888 crore, about $940.45 million) for the quarter ended September 30, from Rs 67.92 billion (Rs 6,792 crore) a year ago, Reuters said. Analysts, on average, had expected a profit of Rs 96.73 billion (Rs 9,673 crore), according to LSEG-compiled data — an expectation, not a reported figure, and the gap between the two is the story.

Where the money went

Forbes India, reporting the same results, put revenue from operations up 16.7 percent to Rs 60,878 crore, and consolidated EBITDA up 17.8 percent to Rs 35,240 crore, for an EBITDA margin of 57.9 percent. It reported network operating costs rose 11 percent and licence fees increased 13 percent — the two cost lines Reuters also cited for the miss.

Airtel spent Rs 12,467 crore on consolidated capital expenditure during the quarter, including Rs 9,908 crore in India, and added 497 towers and 11,684 mobile broadband base stations in the country, Forbes India reported. It also invested Rs 2,826 crore in a strategic land parcel for its data-centre business, part of a plan to build 1 GW of data-centre capacity.

"Our investment in a strategic land parcel during the quarter marks another important step towards realising our ambition of building 1 GW of data centre capacity."

— Gopal Vittal, executive vice-chairman, Bharti Airtel

The operating numbers underneath

India business revenue was Rs 42,308 crore, up 9.4 percent year-on-year, with mobile revenue up 10.1 percent, Forbes India reported. Average revenue per user (ARPU) rose to Rs 271 from Rs 256 a year earlier, which Airtel attributed to premiumisation and acquiring higher-value customers. Airtel reported 693 million customers across its India and Africa businesses in 15 countries; Africa had 193.9 million customers and revenue there grew 20.6 percent year-on-year in constant-currency terms.

The postpaid push is visible in the detail. Airtel added 1.2 million postpaid customers during the quarter — its highest quarterly addition — taking the postpaid base to 31.2 million, and added 2.9 million smartphone data customers sequentially, Forbes India reported. Its homes business added 676,000 customers to reach 15.4 million, with revenue up 25.3 percent.

Market context

Airtel shares closed at Rs 2,062.05 on the BSE on Thursday, down 0.19 percent, before the results announcement, Forbes India reported — so the share reaction to the miss itself comes in the next session. For comparison, the same report noted Reliance Jio's mobile ARPU was Rs 218.8 for the quarter, below Airtel's Rs 271, and that TRAI data for September showed Jio adding 2.713 million wireless subscribers against Airtel's 2.692 million.

What to watch next

Two questions decide whether the miss is a blip. First, costs: whether network operating costs and licence fees keep growing faster than revenue. Second, pricing: whether premiumisation alone can keep lifting ARPU from Rs 271 without a broad tariff increase. The next quarterly results, and the market's reaction in the first session after this announcement, are the immediate checkpoints for investors holding Airtel in India portfolios.
